record.title: Classification of spreads yielding projectively inequivalent hyperovals
record.statement: Let ${\cal S}$ be a spread containing $t_N$ and $t_\infty$, whose other lines each meet exactly one ${\cal C}$-line. **Classification of inequivalent hyperovals.** Which regular spreads give projectively inequivalent hyperovals? This is posed among the paper's open questions about classifying the sets ${\cal C}$ and their corresponding spreads. No answer or resolution is supplied in the source.
record.source_name: S. G. Barwick and Wen-Ai Jackson, “A characterisation of translation ovals in finite even order planes”, arXiv:1305.6673 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1305.6673

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2013).

record.title: The planar strip occupancy conjecture
record.statement: Let $N$ be a positive integer and let $x_1,\ldots,x_N$ be points in the unit disk in the plane. A strip of width $1/N$ is a planar strip with that width. **Planar strip occupancy conjecture.** There is a function $g$ on the positive integers tending to infinity such that, for any $N$ points in the unit disk on the plane, there is a strip of width $1/N$ containing at least $g(N)$ of the given points. This is the planar analogue of the spherical strip question, asking for an unbounded lower bound on the number of points captured by a strip of reciprocal width; the source poses it as an open question.
record.source_name: Nóra Frankl, János Nagy and Márton Naszódi, “Coverings: variations on a result of Rogers and on the Epsilon-net theorem of Haussler and Welzl”, arXiv:1607.02888 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1607.02888

Status: **open** according to the source (as of July 2016). “We pose the following open questions:”

record.title: The rainbow 2-factor conjecture for properly colored complete graphs
record.statement:
Let $K_{2n}$ be a complete graph with a proper edge-coloring using exactly $2n-1$ colors. A **multicolored $2$-factor** is a $2$-factor whose edges have pairwise distinct colors. **The rainbow 2-factor conjecture.** Every proper edge-coloring of $K_{2n}$ by $2n-1$ colors contains a multicolored $2$-factor on either $2n-1$ or $2n$ vertices.

This is an anti-Ramsey-type strengthening of the fact that sufficiently many colors force a multicolored $1$-factor. The two allowed orders account for parity issues, and the paper proposes the assertion as an open problem.
record.source_name: János Barát and Zoltán Lóránt Nagy, “Transversals in generalized Latin squares”, arXiv:1701.08220 (2017).

record.title: Sands–Sauer–Woodrow stable-set domination problem for quasi-order multidigraphs
record.statement:
Let $D$ be a multidigraph whose arcs are the union of $k$ quasi-orders. A **stable set** is a set of vertices containing no arc between distinct vertices, and a dominating set $S$ satisfies $N^+(S)=V(D)$. **Sands–Sauer–Woodrow stable-set domination problem.** For every $k$, there exists an integer $f(k)$ such that $D$ has a dominating set which is the union of $f(k)$ stable sets.

This is a more general open problem than the complete-multidigraph formulation and has been investigated in the cited literature. The paper states that it remains open.
record.source_name: N. Bousquet, W. Lochet and S. Thomassé, “A proof of the Erdős-Sands-Sauer-Woodrow conjecture”, arXiv:1703.08123 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1703.08123

Status: **open** according to the source (as of March 2017). “Despite some attention (see , , , , for example) the case $k=3$ was still open in both conjectures.”

record.title: Every Hist-snark has a cycle double cover containing all outer cycles
record.statement: Let a **Hist-snark** be a snark with a Hist, where a Hist is a spanning tree having only vertices of degree three and one, and the outer cycles are the vertex-disjoint cycles induced by the edges outside the Hist. A **cycle double cover** is a collection of cycles such that every edge is contained in exactly two cycles. **Cycle double-cover conjecture for Hist-snarks.** Every Hist-snark has a cycle double cover which contains all outer cycles. This is posed as an open problem about cycle double covers of snarks with special spanning trees; the source gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Arthur Hoffmann-Ostenhof and Thomas Jatschka, “Snarks with special spanning trees”, arXiv:1706.05595 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.05595

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2017).

record.title: The bipartite directed perfect-matching conjecture
record.statement: Let $G$ be a 3-connected, cubic, bipartite digraph. A **perfect matching without a directed cut** is a perfect matching that contains no directed cut. **Bipartite directed perfect-matching conjecture.** $G$ contains a perfect matching without a directed cut. The paper presents this as a new question arising naturally from the preceding framework; no resolution is given.
record.source_name: Kolja Knauer and Petru Valicov, “Cuts in matchings of 3-connected cubic graphs”, arXiv:1712.06143 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1712.06143

record.title: Open-subgroup triviality conjecture for word values
record.statement:
Let $w=w(x_1,\ldots,x_r)$ be a group word and let $G$ be a profinite group. Write $w(H)$ for the closed subgroup generated by the $w$-values in a subgroup $H$.

**Open-subgroup triviality conjecture.** If

$$
|G_w|<2^{\aleph_0},
$$

then there is an open subgroup $H$ of $G$ such that

$$
w(H)=1.
$$

This is presented as another weaker version of the strong conciseness conjecture. Its general validity is not proved in the paper and remains open.
record.source_name: Eloisa Detomi, Benjamin Klopsch and Pavel Shumyatsky, “Strong conciseness in profinite groups”, arXiv:1907.01344 (2020).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2013–2019). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1306.5970](https://arxiv.org/abs/1306.5970).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.01344

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2019).

record.title: Equivariant partite-presentation refinement for vertex transitive graphs
record.statement:
Let $\Gha$ be a vertex transitive graph with a partite presentation $P$ such that $\Gha=\operatorname{PCay}(P)$, and let $\Gpa\leq\operatorname{Aut}_{c\text{-}loc}(\Gha)$ be a transitive group. A **cover** is a graph map $\eta:\Gha\to\sC_{P'}$ compatible with the stated presentation structure. **Equivariant presentation conjecture.** There exists a partite presentation $P'$ such that $\Gha=\operatorname{PCay}(P')$, together with a cover $\eta:\Gha\to\sC_{P'}$ and a homomorphism $\phi:\Gpa\to\operatorname{Aut}(\sC_{P'})$ satisfying

$$
\eta(g\cdot x)=\phi(g)\cdot\eta(x)
$$

for $x\in V(\Gha)\cup\overrightarrow{E}(\Gha)$. Thus the action of $\Gpa$ commutes with the cover. The source presents this as a possible generalisation of the procedure, but does not explicitly label it as an open conjecture.
record.source_name: Agelos Georgakopoulos, Matthias Hamann and Alex Wendland, “Presentations for Vertex Transitive Graphs”, arXiv:2007.06432 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2007.06432

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2020).

record.title: Realizability of all orders among graph thresholds
record.statement:
For a graph $H$, let $\delta_\chi(H)$ and $\delta_{\hom}(H)$ be its chromatic and homomorphism thresholds, and let $\delta_{\mathrm{lin\mhyphen rem}}(H)$ and $\delta_{\mathrm{poly\mhyphen rem}}(H)$ be its linear and polynomial removal thresholds. **Realizability conjecture for the four thresholds.** There exists a graph $H$ for which

$$
\delta_\chi(H),\delta_{\hom}(H),\delta_{\mathrm{lin\mhyphen rem}}(H),\delta_{\mathrm{poly\mhyphen rem}}(H)
$$

are all distinct. More generally, these four numbers may appear in any order in $[0,1]$, subject to

$$
\delta_\chi(H)\leq\delta_{\hom}(H)\qquad\text{and}\qquad\delta_{\mathrm{poly\mhyphen rem}}(H)\leq\delta_{\mathrm{lin\mhyphen rem}}(H).
$$

This is posed as an open question inspired by the Allen--Böttcher--Griffiths--Kohayakawa--Morris theorem; the claimed realizability of all admissible orders remains open.
record.source_name: Jacob Fox and Yuval Wigderson, “Minimum degree and the graph removal lemma”, arXiv:2105.09194 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2105.09194

Status: **open** according to the source (as of May 2021). “But we do leave the following open question, inspired by the Allen--B\"ottcher--Griffiths--Kohayakawa--Morris theorem.”

record.title: The stability conjecture for infinite set-homogeneous hypergraphs
record.statement:
Let $k\geq 3$, and let $H$ be an infinite set-homogeneous $k$-hypergraph whose theory is **stable**, meaning that it does not have the order property: there are no formula $\phi(\bar{x},\bar{y})$, model $M$, and sequences $(\bar{a}_i)_{i\in\omega}$ and $(\bar{b}_j)_{j\in\omega}$ such that $M\models\phi(\bar{a}_i,\bar{b}_j)$ if and only if $i<j$. A $k$-hypergraph is **complete** if every $k$-element subset is a hyperedge, and its **complete complement** is obtained by replacing the hyperedge relation with its complement.

**The stability conjecture.** Any infinite set-homogeneous $k$-hypergraph with stable theory is complete or has complete complement.

This predicts that stability forces an infinite set-homogeneous $k$-hypergraph to be trivial up to complementation. The supplied text poses the statement without indicating whether it is known or resolved.
record.source_name: Amir Assari, Narges Hosseinzadeh and Dugald Macpherson, “Set-homogeneous hypergraphs”, arXiv:2202.09613 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.09613

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2022).

record.title: The colorability-extension conjecture for uniform bi-hypergraphs
record.statement:
Let $Bi\mathcal{H}yp(n,r,m)$ denote the class of $r$-uniform bi-hypergraphs of order $n$ and size $m$. Assume $r\ge 3$ and $n\ge (r-1)^2+1$.

**Colorability-extension conjecture.** For any $r,m,n\in \mathbb{N}$ with $r\ge 3$ and $n\ge (r-1)^2+1$, if all bi-hypergraphs in $Bi\mathcal{H}yp(n,r,m)$ are colorable, then all bi-hypergraphs in $Bi\mathcal{H}yp(n+1,r,m)$ are also colorable.

The source notes that an analogous extension result was proved under restrictions in the $r=4$ case, and asks whether the conclusion holds without those restrictions. The unrestricted statement is left unresolved.
record.source_name: Meiqiao Zhang, Fengming Dong and Ruixue Zhang, “On the colorability of bi-hypergraphs”, arXiv:2310.06464 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.06464

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2023).

record.title: The self-avoiding-walk bunkbed question
record.statement:
Suppose $G=(V,E)$ is a finite, connected, simple graph. For $x,y\in V$, let $\mathscr{S}(x,y)$ be the set of self-avoiding walks from $x$ to $y$, and let $\mathscr{S}(u_i,v_j)$ denote the corresponding set on $G\times K_2$. **Self-avoiding-walk bunkbed question.** Is it true that for all distinct $u,v\in V(G)$,

$$
\big|\mathscr{S}(u_0,v_0)\big|\leq \big|\mathscr{S}(u_0,v_1)\big|?
$$

The question has a negative answer in general: the inequality fails for ladder graphs, although it holds for complete bunkbed graphs $K_n\times K_2$ for all $n\geq 3$ by the stated theorem. Therefore the proposed assertion is refuted.
record.source_name: Pengfei Tang, “Maximum flow and self-avoiding walk on bunkbed graphs”, arXiv:2502.06237 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.06237

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of February 2025). “This conjecture was first proposed---albeit in a slightly different formulation---by Kasteleyn and was recently proved false .”

record.title: NP-completeness conjecture for regular completions of trees
record.statement: Let $T$ be a tree of maximum degree $\Delta$. For $d\geq\Delta$, let $\overline{T_d}$ be a $d$-regular graph obtained from $T$ by adding semi-edges or loops so that every vertex of $\overline{T_d}$ has degree $d$; this graph is not uniquely determined. **Regular-tree completion conjecture.** If $\Delta\geq 3$ and $\overline{T_d}$ is constructed as above, then the $\textsc{\overline{T_d}-Cover}$ problem is NP-complete even for simple input graphs. This is proposed as an open question arising from the paper's results, and its proof is described as a further goal.
record.source_name: Jan Bok, Jiří Fiala, Nikola Jedličková and Jan Kratochvíl, “Computational complexity of covering regular trees”, arXiv:2507.00564 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.00564

Status: **open** according to the source (as of July 2025).

record.title: Precoloring extension conjecture for Cartesian products with complete bipartite graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a bipartite graph with maximum degree $\Delta(G)$, and let $K_{n,m}$ be a complete bipartite graph with $n\geq m$. Consider a precoloring of some edges of the Cartesian product $G\square K_{n,m}$ using at most $\Delta(G)+n$ colors, with the distance between every two precolored edges at least $2$.

**Cartesian-product precoloring extension conjecture.** This precoloring is extendable to a proper edge coloring.

This is proposed as a possible generalization of the paper's hypercube result and is presented as a question about whether the analogous theorem holds for Cartesian products with complete bipartite graphs. The source gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Pál Bärnkopf, “Extending edge-colorings of distance-2 matchings in the hypercube”, arXiv:2509.15764 (2026).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.15764

record.title: Necessary and sufficient conditions for scatteredness of the generalized quadrinomial
record.statement:
Let $t\geq 3$, let $1\leq s\leq 2t-1$, and let $m\in\mathbb F_{q^t}$ and $h\in\mathbb F_{q^{2t}}$. Consider the $q^s$-polynomial

$$
\psi_{m,h,s}=m\left(X^{q^s}-h^{1-q^{s(t-1)}}X^{q^{s(t-1)}}\right)+X^{q^{s(t+1)}}+h^{1-q^{s(2t-1)}}X^{q^{s(2t-1)}}\in\widetilde{\mathcal L}_{n,q,s}.
$$

**Scatteredness conjecture.** The polynomial $\psi_{m,h,s}$ is scattered if and only if $m$ and $h$ satisfy the assumptions in Theorem~.

The conjecture asserts that the sufficient conditions established in Theorem~ are also necessary. The paper reports computational evidence for this necessity, while the general equivalence remains open.
record.source_name: Alessandro Giannoni, Giovanni Giuseppe Grimaldi, Giovanni Longobardi and Marco Timpanella, “Generalizing a family of scattered quadrinomials in F_q^2t[X]”, arXiv:2601.09415 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.09415

Status: **open** according to the source (as of January 2026). “We conclude this section with the following open problem.”

record.title: Distinguishing conjecture for distinct immersion-closed classes
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{M}_1$ and $\mathcal{M}_2$ be two distinct immersion-closed and union-closed graph classes. For graphs $G$ and $H$, write $G =_{\mathcal{M}} H$ when $\hom(K,G)=\hom(K,H)$ for every $K\in\mathcal{M}$. **Distinguishing conjecture.** There exist $i,j\in\{1,2\}$ with $i\ne j$ and graphs $G$ and $H$ such that

$$
G =_{\mathcal{M}_i} H \quad\text{and}\quad G \ne_{\mathcal{M}_j} H.
$$

This would strengthen the paper's homomorphism-counting results by showing that distinct immersion-closed, union-closed classes induce genuinely different equivalence relations. The source presents it as an open problem, and no resolution is specified.
record.source_name: Andrea Jiménez, Benjamin Moore, Daniel A. Quiroz and Youngho Yoo, “Homomorphism counting for immersion-closed classes is not isomorphism”, arXiv:2602.08738 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.08738

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2026).

record.title: Ambient cubic-container problem for visibility cliques
record.statement:
Let $A\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ be a finite point set. A **visibility patch** is a subset $W\subset\Gamma(\mathbb{R})$ of a real cubic on which the relevant pairs of points are considered, and an ambient blocker for a pair from $A\cap W$ is a point of $A\setminus\Gamma$ lying in the open segment joining that pair. **Ambient cubic-container problem.** For every $k,\ell$ there are constants $\alpha>0$ and $\beta<1/(\ell-1)$ such that, if $A\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ has $n$ points, no $k$ collinear points, and no $\ell$ mutually visible points, then there is a real cubic $\Gamma$ and a visibility patch $W\subset\Gamma(\mathbb{R})$ for which

$$
|A\cap W|\ge \alpha n
$$

and the number of ambient blockers in $A\setminus\Gamma$ for pairs from $A\cap W$ is at most

$$
\beta |A\cap W|.
$$

This is identified as the missing ambient container theorem that could combine with the paper's cubic-container result to prove the Big-Line–Big-Clique Conjecture. It is posed as an open problem.
record.source_name: Sohail Sarkar, “Visibility cliques, cubic containers, and dense orchard cores”, arXiv:2605.00918 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.00918

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2026).

record.title: Hindman's monochromatic sum-product quadruple question
record.statement:
Let a finite partition of $\mathbb{N}$ be given. **Hindman's question.** There exist $x,y\in\mathbb{N}$ such that

$$
\{x,y,x+y,xy\}
$$

is monochromatic. This asks whether every finite coloring of the positive integers contains a monochromatic configuration simultaneously involving two numbers, their sum, and their product.
record.source_name: Conner Griffin, “Infinite Sum-Product Configurations in Parallel”, arXiv:2605.24751 (2026).
record.references:

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.24751

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2026).

record.title: Polynomial-size grid drawing problem for planar graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be an arbitrary planar graph. A **proper grid drawing** of $G$ is a drawing in which vertices are represented by grid points and edges by noncrossing straight-line segments, with no grid point representing a vertex lying in the interior of an edge. Is there a proper grid drawing of $G$ in a grid of polynomial size?

**Polynomial-size grid drawing problem.** For every planar graph $G$, there is a proper grid drawing of $G$ in a grid of polynomial size.

The paper presents this as an open question because polynomial-size proper grid drawings are known for bounded-degree planar graphs, while the general case remains unresolved.
record.source_name: Martin Balko, “Grid Representations and the Chromatic Number”, arXiv:1204.0210 (2012).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1204.0210

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2012).

record.title: Open problems on cyclic cycle decompositions of nearly complete 3-uniform hypergraphs
record.statement:
Let $K_v^{(3)}$ be the complete $3$-uniform hypergraph on vertex set $\mathbb{Z}_v$, and let $I$ consist of the missing triplets $(i,i+v/3,i+2v/3)$ whenever $3\mid v$. A decomposition is **cyclic** if translation $i\mapsto i+1\pmod v$ is an automorphism. A decomposition is **2-split** if it has the 2-split structure described earlier in the paper. The authors pose the following four problems. **Cyclic decomposition problems.** (i) For every $v\equiv 0,3,6\pmod {12}$ with $v\geq 6$, there exists a cyclic $6$-cycle decomposition of

$$
K_v^{(3)}-I.
$$

(ii) For every $v\equiv 0,6,12\pmod {24}$ with $v\geq 12$, there exists a cyclic 2-split $6$-cycle decomposition of $K_v^{(3)}-I$. (iii) For every $v\equiv 0\pmod 3$ with $v\geq 9$, there exists a cyclic $9$-cycle decomposition of $K_v^{(3)}-I$. (iv) For every $v\equiv 0\pmod 6$ with $v\geq 18$, there exists a cyclic 2-split $9$-cycle decomposition of $K_v^{(3)}-I$. These problems concern imposing cyclic symmetry, and remain open although the unrestricted decomposition spectrum has been completely determined.
record.source_name: Anita Keszler and Zsolt Tuza, “Spectrum of 3-uniform 6- and 9-cycle systems over K_v^(3)-I”, arXiv:2212.11058 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.11058

Status: **open** according to the source (as of December 2022). “Concerning cyclic cyctems we formulate the following open problems.”
